g1_mech#2.closest: US4818148 "Frost damage proofed pile", plus bitumen-coat negative-skin-friction work (Canadian patent CA1254393 family; TRID "Performance of bituminous coats in reducing negative skin friction")
g1_mech#2.same: Piles in permafrost with a smooth slip covering on the shaft. Bitumen coats cut negative skin friction and downdrag. Soviet and Norilsk piles use end-bearing and rock-bearing design.
g1_mech#2.new: The combined package for thaw: a bored rock socket below the frozen layer, a bitumen sleeve over the frozen zone only, and load-cell monitoring over 3–5 thaw seasons. I found no permafrost-thaw-specific case with all three. The search did not reach SP 25.13330 or Russian-language sources.

g1_ledger#1.closest: Novatek "Ob LNG", 2 trains of 2.5 Mtpa on the modified Arctic Cascade (ACM), plus the ACM patent for 3 Mtpa trains on domestic equipment, Novatek, 2019–2020
g1_ledger#1.same: Mid-scale (2.5–3 Mtpa) Arctic Cascade trains, designed to use domestic equipment, built in parallel on a gravity base.
g1_ledger#1.new: Sizing at 1.5–2.5 Mtpa, with 3–4 trains each starting up as built after the 2022 import loss. I found no published uptime or cost data for it. The Ob LNG FID and build status are unconfirmed.

g1_rf1#2.closest: Novatek's Saam FSU (Ura Bay) and Kildin/Murmansk transshipment complex, plus the Arc7 winter shuttle plan, Novatek/Arctic Transshipment, 2020–2026
g1_rf1#2.same: Arc7 carriers shuttle to Murmansk-area floating storage, and conventional tankers carry the LNG onward. Novatek planned a 4-day turnaround to support winter shuttles to Murmansk, and is building 360,000 m³ storage units at Murmansk and Kamchatka.
g1_rf1#2.new: Nothing in the mechanism. Only the specific 1.5–2x tonnage estimate and turnaround logging are new.

g1_rf1#1.closest: Yamal LNG Train 4 (Arctic Cascade, 0.9 Mtpa, started May 2021), Novatek; also the Ob LNG ACM design
g1_rf1#1.same: The domestic 0.9 Mtpa Arctic Cascade train exists and runs. Novatek has used the same approach on gravity bases with shared port facilities. Cryogas-Vysotsk at 0.66 Mtpa is another small-train precedent.
g1_rf1#1.new: Copying the 0.9 Mtpa train in series at Utrenneye and Sabetta, sharing the existing infrastructure, with the sub-$600/t/y capex target. I found no published plan or cost data.

g1_rf2#3.closest: ARCO North Slope passive subgrade cooling with 29 installations, including retrofits (CPC5-365); the Qinghai–Tibet line piles retrofitted with thermosyphons, 7 years of monitoring (Permafrost and Periglacial Processes 33(3), 2022)
g1_rf2#3.same: Retrofitting thermosyphons to existing piles, with monitoring of the result. Nornickel runs foundation geotechnical monitoring since 2020. InSAR was used on the 2020 tank collapse (Remote Sensing 14(19):5036).
g1_rf2#3.new: Ranking Norilsk and Talnakh structures by InSAR plus borehole data to decide which get retrofits, with a cutoff at a 40% capacity loss. I found no such ranking method.

g1_ledger#3.closest: US11555658B2 "Methods and systems to convert passive cooling to active cooling"
g1_ledger#3.same: A chiller circulates glycol coolant through pile or thermosyphon tubing, runs in summer, and does not depend on the weather. Also Univ. of Alberta glycol screw-pile work and CCHRC "Pile Adfreeze with Active Refrigeration".
g1_ledger#3.new: Using the LNG plant's own refrigeration as the cold source, applying the loop to pile caps, and the 5 W/m² and 2.5 MW sizing. I found no LNG-plant use.
